title: JPCUB Competitive Landscape v2.0: System-Level Joules-per-Solution Estimates for 17 Quantum Computing Platforms from Pub
description: Companion paper to JPCUB P0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21637028). Computes joules-per-solution (JPCUB) estimates for 17 quantum computing platforms from published specifications: 13 gate-model (7 superconducting, 4 trapped-ion, 2 neutral-atom) plus 2 annealing, 1 photonic, and 1 pre-commercial target. Key finding: gate speed dominates joules-per-solution. Superconducting platforms (0.05-0.71 J/sol) lead via 30-500 ns gates; neutral atoms (0.32-0.62 J/sol) balance Rydberg-gate speed with room-temperature operation; trapped ions (8.5-16.3 J/sol) rank last because 50-100 us gate times overwhelm the room-temperature power advantage. Only IBM Eagle has a published JPCUB (0.89 J/sol, P0). All other values are conservative system-level upper bounds pending independent measurement per JPCUB P0 adversarial validation provisions. Includes reproducible computation script and full specification-source trac
